strategy_roster.name: Precipice Martin Strategy (C#)
strategy_roster.notes: Non-trading: the documented grid opens an alternating long/short market order on every finished candle with pip-based SL/TP and martingale sizing, so it contains no market-derived directional entry signal to translate. Marked with a never-true guard.

strategy_roster.name: Three Supertrend EMA
strategy_roster.entry_long: close > ema(close,10) and close > ema(close,20) and close > ema(close,50)
strategy_roster.notes: SuperTrend is not in the DSL, so each of the three lines is proxied by its own EMA and the documented EMA filter by the slowest line; periods 10/20/50 are explicit fallbacks. Exit is the documented flip of the fastest line, and no stops are documented.

strategy_roster.name: MA Crossover with TP/SL and 5 EMA Filter
strategy_roster.notes: Keeps the documented long rule: fast SMA crossing above the slow SMA while close is above the 5-period EMA, with the opposite cross or EMA loss as exit. Fast 20 and slow 50 are explicit fallbacks, and Target%/Stop% carry no documented values, so both stop fields are null.

strategy_roster.name: Bollinger Bands N Positions v2
strategy_roster.notes: Envelope breakouts are expressed with Bollinger 20/2 (period and deviation have no documented defaults, so they are explicit fallbacks); the mean reversion back to bb_mid is used as the long exit. Pyramiding, netting, and the pip-based stop/target/trailing pair are not expressible, so the stop fields are null.

strategy_roster.name: ZeroLag MACD Cross
strategy_roster.notes: The documented FastEmaLength 2, SlowEmaLength 34 and SignalEmaLength 2 are used directly, and crossabove/crossbelow already enforce the documented UseFreshSignal requirement. Session hours 9-15, the KillDay/KillHour forced exit and Volume are not expressible, and the docs state there are no stops.

strategy_roster.name: Nova
strategy_roster.entry_long: close > open and roc(close,1) > 1.0 and roc(close,1) > roc(close,2)
strategy_roster.notes: The Level1 ask-versus-stored-ask test is approximated on bars as a bullish candle that has gained more than 1% and is accelerating, with the reverse as exit. StepPips 1% is an explicit fallback; the seconds-based snapshot, StopLossPips/TakeProfitPips and LossCoefficient sizing are not expressible.

strategy_roster.name: TSI Long Short for BTC 2H
strategy_roster.notes: True Strength Index is not in the DSL, so it is proxied by ROC(25) (explicit fallback) and the documented Highest/Lowest extremes become 100-bar Donchian levels on that proxy, with prior-bar levels used since the current bar cannot exceed its own window. The 2-hour timeframe and short side are dropped.

strategy_roster.name: Billy Expert Pullback Buyer
strategy_roster.entry_long: close < donchian_high_prev(high,10) and rsi(close,14) > 50 and roc(rsi(close,14),1) > 0
strategy_roster.notes: The sequence of falling highs becomes a pullback below the 10-bar high and the two higher-timeframe bullish stochastics are approximated by RSI(14) above 50 and rising (periods are fallbacks). Stacking up to MaxPositions 6 is not supported, and StopLossPips 0 / TakeProfitPips 32 are pip distances, so the stop fields are null.

strategy_roster.name: AutoTrading Scheduler
strategy_roster.notes: Non-trading: the documented module is an explicitly signal-agnostic weekly schedule supervisor that only toggles auto trading and flattens positions, so it defines no market-derived entry. Marked with a never-true guard.

strategy_roster.name: Oscillator Evaluator
strategy_roster.notes: The stochastic oscillator is expressed as a %K-style position inside the 14-bar Donchian range; a flat range makes the ratio infinite rather than an error, and such bars simply fail the comparison. Both oscillators must be oversold to enter and neutral to exit, with 30/20/50 levels as explicit fallbacks since no thresholds are documented.
